staging_observations: Both complete drawn panels inspected. Setup establishes occupied chair/feet/snack relations; chase establishes vacant chair, four-legged airborne dog and separated actor/stunt performers. Final chase correctly removes the staging collar.

images.inspection: Opened complete image at original/native output resolution using view_image detail=original.
findings: Neet has a full narrow connected torso, fine legs, broad triangular ears, projecting muzzle and short nub. His four feet are planted with coherent limb ownership; the snack-directed upward gaze makes the setup legible.

Buddy retains a moderately elongated connected trunk, neck, substantial legs and clearance. The chair X braces occlude parts of his torso and far limbs consistently; four dog feet remain distinguishable from the chair feet and the seated man's shoes. No disconnected limb or unsupported body is visible.

Heather holds both leash origins. Neet's clip/collar connection is clear. Buddy's slack lead crosses in front of the torso, is interrupted by the foreground chair brace, and can continue to his collar behind the nearer brace/head; it is not visibly knotted or attached to the chair. This overlap is busy but physically plausible.

Buddy's charcoal body is a close smooth mass with small natural edge accents, not raised shag volume or engraved curls. Furnished ears, pale muzzle and brows remain regional. Neet's broad paint variation does not read as long patterned body hair.

Occupied chair, snack table, samosas, park and film equipment match the exact pre-sitting story state. Human feet and perspective remain plausible; cropped Heather is provisional. Warm finish and two competing sightlines provide a readable comedy setup.

images.inspection: Opened complete image at original/native output resolution using view_image detail=original.
findings: Neet's projecting mouth grips a visible tuft of the overturned stitched plush retriever. His grounded near foreleg and two hind legs support him while the far forepaw bends upward beside the toy. Limb roots and torso are continuous; the lifted paw is not a detached extra limb.

Broad smooth fawn tonal planes preserve Neet's short coat and narrow full trunk, large triangular ears and tiny nub. The plush alone carries deliberately long fluffy texture, making the mistaken opponent immediately distinguishable.

Buddy has four grounded substantial legs, belly clearance, an elongated connected charcoal torso and a modest furnished face. Close body planes remain distinct from brows, beard, ear and distal-paw furnishings; no material body shag remains.

Camera, light, case and cable support the park film set. Buddy keeps clear of the cable and observes at a sensible distance. Neet has no collar after slipping out. The toppled prop precedes the scoop-up and the image contributes the central physical gag rather than repeating the setup.

images.inspection: Opened complete image at original/native output resolution using view_image detail=original.
findings: Neet's extended airborne run has four separately owned legs attached to continuous shoulder and hindquarter structures. The projecting muzzle, triangular ears, fine limbs, full slim torso and tiny nub remain recognizable. No collar or leash persists after the escape.

Buddy is smaller in the composition but has visible connected shoulders/chest, substantial grounded legs and real clearance beneath his body. Chair braces pass in front without generating false dog limbs; the dog remains planted beneath the empty seat.

At native image size Buddy's cream moustache/beard, pale brows and furnished pendant ears remain recognizable. His smooth charcoal torso is distinct from those localized hair regions; tail is tapering with modest fringe, not a plume. No material new curly body texture was introduced by the face edit.

The white-clad actor runs ahead, with two separated stunt performers behind Neet. Human limb ownership and action spacing are plausible; nobody collides with the dog. The empty chair pays off Buddy's view-taking thread and is consistent with the earlier dark chair.

Park daylight, relative depth, ground shadows and overall finish are coherent. The chase offers a broad action composition distinct from the close prop scene. Human appearances remain provisional; this is an illustrated running interpretation, not verified gait evidence.
